title: The duct tape fix that saved Apollo 13
dek: Three astronauts were breathing in their own carbon dioxide. The fix was built from bags and tape.
paragraphs: Apollo 13 launched for the Moon in April 1970 with Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise aboard. On their third day in space, an oxygen tank exploded in the service module. The crew moved into the lunar module, Aquarius, and used it as a lifeboat.

The lunar module was designed for two people, not three. Its lithium hydroxide canisters, which pull carbon dioxide out of the air, couldn't keep up, and the gas began to build. The command module had spare canisters, but they didn't fit the lunar module's system.
Engineers on the ground worked out an adapter using only things the crew had on board: plastic bags, a spacesuit hose, and tape.
It worked. The adapter cleaned the air, and all three astronauts made it home.
takeaway: Improvising works best when you know exactly what you have. Know every item in your kit and what else it can do, and a few supplies become many options.
